subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what metadata should be canonical across protocol, transcripts, events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: This is a product/API/session-state contract rather than a narrow bug fix: current code has several partial attribution mechanisms, and maintainers need to choose one source of truth before implementation.

options.title: Design Additive Sender Metadata
options.body: Add a durable sender identity object with sender id, kind, display name, source session/agent, and renderable avatar/color metadata, then migrate UI and session surfaces to consume it.

options.title: Keep Narrow Partial Fixes
options.body: Continue landing scoped senderLabel, requester-name, and WebChat fallback repairs while leaving the broader durable identity contract unimplemented for now.

options.title: Defer Multi-Agent UI Identity
options.body: Leave this as a roadmap item until a broader multi-agent/session model design is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Sender Metadata
recommendation.body: Add a durable sender identity object with sender id, kind, display name, source session/agent, and renderable avatar/color metadata, then migrate UI and session surfaces to consume it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provenance, sessions, Gateway protocol, transcript semantics, and product direction, and steipete has the strongest history and prior review context on those surfaces.
